action: Microsoft advises searching mail telemetry for the published sender domains and subject patterns, quarantining matches, and, for anyone who may have entered credentials, resetting the password and revoking sessions and tokens.
exec: Criminals are using a real outage to make scam emails convincing, raising the risk of stolen staff logins.
plain: Scammers are sending fake Microsoft 365 service notices that claim messages were held after an outage, according to Microsoft.

key_findings: Microsoft observed a high-volume phishing campaign on November 13 aimed at organisations in multiple sectors worldwide.
Emails use subjects like 'Outage' plus a random token and sender names posing as service-health notices, claiming four messages were held after a November 12 Exchange Online incident.
A 'RESTORE MESSAGES' button leads to a likely credential-phishing page; Microsoft has not confirmed credential capture.
Randomised subjects, recipient-specific tracking links and rotating sender domains are used to defeat simple pattern matching.
Microsoft has not attributed the campaign to a named actor or malware family.
recommendations: Search mail telemetry for the published sender domains, subject patterns and lure phrases, then quarantine and remove delivered copies.
Identify users who clicked using click, proxy and endpoint logs.
For anyone who may have entered credentials, reset the password, revoke sessions and tokens, verify MFA registrations and review inbox rules and OAuth grants.
Turn on Safe Links, Safe Attachments and zero-hour auto purge, and prefer phishing-resistant MFA.
Remind users that genuine service-health notices do not point to non-Microsoft sites; check the Microsoft 365 admin center.

summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes a high-volume phishing campaign seen on November 13 that poses as Microsoft 365 service-health notices claiming messages were held after a November 12 Exchange Online incident. Microsoft has not named an actor or confirmed credential capture. KnowBe4 reported that on November 13 outage-related phishing emails reached about 468 times the November 9 to 11 daily average in detections.
title: Phishing campaign uses the Microsoft 365 outage as a lure

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Microsoft Threat Intelligence report. The incident number EX1550543 appears only in an AI-assisted forum post, not in Microsoft's post, so it is not asserted here. KnowBe4 Threat Lab (24 November) independently reports outage-themed phishing on November 13.

date_note: Date of Microsoft's post; the campaign was observed on November 13.

review.note: plain said 'threaten to delete held emails' (not in summary or source); action now names Microsoft and matches its advice (credentials 'may have' been entered). Date, 468x figure and status checked against Microsoft and KnowBe4.

evidence.quote: On Nov. 13, outage-related phishing emails reached about 468 times the Nov. 9 to Nov. 11 daily average in detections
